table.title: Chinese Government Secured Foreign Loans
table.caption_extra: Outstanding January 1, 1932. Compiled by E. Kann, Shanghai, and J. Baylin, Tientsin. Under care of Ministry of Finance. C=Capital I=Interest

rows: Chinese Imp. Government 5% Gold Loan of 1896 (Anglo-German)
Redeemable by annual drawings of 1,04345% for capital and interest. Final redemption April 1, 1932.
Chinese Imp. Government 4½% Gold Loan of 1898 (Anglo-German)
Redeemable by annual drawings of 0.7202018% for sinking fund. Final payment March 1, 1943.
Chinese Government 5% Reorganization Gold Loan of 1913

Issued in London £7,416,680, Paris £7,416,660, Berlin £6,000,000, Petersburg £2,777,780, Brussels £1,388,880 in 5 currencies on the basis of 1£ = 25.25 = Mks. Frs. 20.45 = Rbls. = Yen 9.796 (9.47). Redeemable by 37 annual drawings from 1924 onwards; final redemption July 1, 1960. Secured on Salt Gabelle and Surplus Customs Revenue, subject to existing prior rights. Actually provided for by the Customs Revenue, subject to existing prior rights. Nos. 586,668-725,556 of the Russian (yellow) bonds issue has been declared void.
Chinese Republic 5% Gold Loan of 1925 (Banque Industrielle)

Balance of French Boxer Indemnity converted into loan bonds for satisfying claims of Far Eastern creditors of the defunct Banque Industrielle de Chine, and for educational purposes. Final redemption on January 15, 1948. Nos. 532,669-785,000 have the British Bourse Stamp and are counted at the rate of 5 U.S. $ = 1 £.

table.title: Chinese Government Secured Foreign Loans

rows: Balance of converted Belgian Boxer Indemnity. Proceeds of bonds to be devoted to the extent of: 40% to extension and repairs to Lunghai Railway, 35% to construction of other railways in China, 25% to educational and charitable purposes. Red. of cap. semi-annually; final payment on Jan. 1, 1941.
Chinese Imp. Government 5% and 4½% Gold Loan of 1908 (Anglo-French)

Redeemable by annual drawings of £250,000 each. Bearing interest at 5% per annum until October 5, 1923, and thereafter at 4½% until final redemption, which is to take place on Oct. 5, 1938. Secured on salt revenue up to Tls. 2,350,000, and besides on sundry taxes of the provinces of Chekiang, Kiangsu, Hupeh and Chihli.
Chinese Imp. Government 5% Hukuang Railway Sinking Fund Gold Loan (of 1911)
C. since 15/6/25 £823,150; I. German coupon 32 since 3/12/26; all coupons after 34, £891,937 since 15/6/1928

Repayable in 40 years by annual drawings, ending June 3, 1952. Secured by a first charge on Salt revenues to the extent of Tls. 950,000 a year; and other provincial taxes, namely the general likin of the Hunan and Hupeh provinces to the extent of H'kwan taels 2,000,000 per annum for each province. If Customs Tariff definitely revised, stipulating abolition of likin, this loan is to become a first charge on the increase of Customs revenue.
Chinese Government 5% Gold Loan of 1912 (Crisp Loan)
Redeemable by annual drawings, commencing in 1923 and terminating in September, 1952. Arrears to be met by the end of 1934.
6% Treasury Notes in Jap. Gold yen for the Compensation of Public Properties and Salt Interests in Tsingtao (1923)
Contracted in Peking on December 1, 1922. Redeemable by half-yearly instalments of Yen 500,000 each, ending March 13, 1938. Secured on Salt surplus and Customs surplus.

table.title: Chinese Government Secured Foreign Loans

rows: Chinese Government 8% Bonds for Refunding Internal and Short-Term Debts (1922)

This is the Japanese portion of the 96 million dollars internal loan of February 11, 1922. Issued with the security of the surplus Salt revenues, and which was redeemable by 13 instalments, beginning January 31, 1923, and ending January 31, 1929.
Chinese Government 5% Gold Loan of 1914 (Pukow Loan)
C. Frs. 2,269,700 from the start / I. Frs. 54,889,899 since 15/2/1921

Redeemable at par by 35 annual drawings beginning March 1, 1930. Nominally secured on certain industrial undertakings, on certain taxes of the Peiping Municipality, and on the alcohol tax North of the Yangtze.
Republic of China 6% Three Year Secured Gold Loan Treasury Notes of 1919

Issued on November 1, 1919, by the Continental and Commercial Trust and Savings Bank of Chicago, re-placing similar notes of 1916. Security first charge upon the entire revenues from the Wine and Tobacco Taxes; also goods taxes in some provinces. Redeemable November 1, 1921.
Republic of China 6% Two Year Secured Gold Loan Treasury Notes of 1919
C. G. $5,500,000 from the start / I. G. $4,845,000 since 1/6/20
Issued on December 1, 1919, by the Pacific Development Corp. Secured on Wine and Tobacco Taxes. As from December 1, 1921, interest has been raised to 8% per annum.
Chinese Government 8% Tenth Year & Treasury Notes of 1919 (Vickers)
Repayable in 5 annual instalments of £360,600 each, between 1925 and 1928 and one instalment of £360,800 on October 1, 1929. No specific security.
Chinese Government 8% Loans of September 30, 1925. (Skoda Loans)
C. £4,806,232 / I. £2,499,240 both from the start

Representing the consolidation of all previous Austrian (Skoda) loans made to China between 1912 and 1922. Nominal security a first mortgage on the title deed tax and other octroi revenues, on the Peiping government income, but invariably defaulted upon. In 1925 another consolidation scheme was turned into effect in terms of which this loan now stands as indicated.
